utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, please be seated. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Good morning to the technical booth, the interpreters, the staff of the registry, counsel for the Prosecution, counsel for the Defence. Here we are again to continue our proceedings, and it is the turn of the Defence for the accused Mr. Zigic to call a witness. So Mr. Stojanovic or Mr. Deretic, which one of you is going to take the floor?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Perhaps before we announce our next witness, it is my duty to notify this Chamber that at the last sitting, the Prosecution tendered a document. It is document 3/249. The Defence is of the opinion that it would be appropriate to address this exhibit before we call in the next witness, as that was our agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps, Ms. Susan Somers, do you wish to comment on this issue?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have not seen or heard from the Defence since the last break; however, in accordance with our indication that we would send the document or consult with the translation services about the document because of the parenthetical, if I'm correct, that was one of the principal objections, that there was, I think -- am I thinking of the same one? The document with Sikirica. Yes, and there was a parenthetical item that was mentioned. We have spoken with the Language Services. They are preparing, it is my understanding, a memorandum on their policy concerning the use of parentheticals, and as soon as we have that back, I'd be very happy to present the -- or ask the translation itself to present to the Chamber its position on how and why these are used. There was, however, also another matter of a motion filed by the Prosecution on Friday concerning today's witness and the Prosecution's position on protective measures. It may require a private session in order to discuss that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Susan Somers, I must tell you that I am completely out of touch. I don't remember the document, and I am not aware of any request that you made last Friday, but perhaps ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I try to be of assistance, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, actually. I think I see for the first time this motion. Yes, Mr. Deretic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I ask the usher to give you the document that was submitted to the Chamber, that is document 3/249. It is an official report compiled on the 4th of July, 1992, and R -- I don't know what R stands for, probably wartime police station -- Prijedor II, and the note was compiled by security commander for Keraterm, as it says here. Of course, this is a photocopy of a document. So, sorry, it is a reserve police station, not a wartime. The R stands for "reserve."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we are making some progress now. Ms. Susan Somers, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, the particular parenthetical notation has been translated both ways in the course of this trial that I have seen in various translations. However, in order to satisfy the concerns that were raised at the time of our seeking to have the document admitted into evidence, having had it identified, I am anticipating, as I indicated, a memorandum from CLSS which hopefully will explain why things are done in a certain way. And I don't -- my observation from the explanation given to me was that it is not a material point, in terms of the parenthetical. That is something that is done on a regular basis. But as not being a member of that particular department of the Tribunal, I feel I cannot comment further and I would ask that the memo be given to us. However, of course, it is our position that we are seeking its admission and if it is necessary to be used today, for, again, identification purposes, in the course of counsel's examination, we urge its admission, so should he need to use it, I don't believe there would be an issue. On the second matter, I am concerned the Chamber has not seen the motion filed. Courtesy copy of course was provided. However, it is a critical motion, I think, that needs to be brought to the Chamber's attention prior to this witness being brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: If I might say so, Ms. Somers, if you file something on Friday --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: -- it's practically a foregone conclusion we are not going to have it on Monday morning, in my experience here. You may have to give -- serve copies to the Chamber particularly, because I haven't seen that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: We did, Your Honour, to the legal officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Well, I have not seen it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I apologise. I can only represent that it -- I am told by my colleague, to the secretary of the legal officer. There had been also a concern raised. Perhaps -- I think it is very important that the Chamber see the motion. It only came to us literally last minute. We were quite concerned about it, enough to seek to revoke to -- to ask the Chamber to rescind protective measures for the upcoming witness. It was faxed to counsel for the Defence on Friday as well, as soon as it was drafted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we are now going from the question of a document to the question of protective measures, so I think we must discuss one thing at a time. Mr. Deretic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we are discussing two very important matters here. The first is the subject that I have raised, and we have provided you a copy of that document at -- and during the last sitting, that is a week last Friday, it was agreed that a decision would be taken regarding that document. If that decision is going to be delayed, I should be told because we still haven't had occasion to make our submissions regarding that official report. So I am asking: Are we leaving that question aside for the moment and then are we passing on to the issue raised by my learned friend opposite?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With regard to the motion, we need to have time to see the motion, so I can't discuss the motion. If there is a written motion, we have to see it, examine it and think it over. The more important question now is the protective measures for the witness we are waiting to come into the courtroom, so that is what we must address.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I should like to ask my colleague, Mr. Stojanovic, to explain our response to the motion of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for giving me the floor. Perhaps my learned friend Ms. Somers did not complete her submission regarding our witness DD/5 but perhaps it would be better to go into a private session because this is, for the moment, a protected witness and the Prosecution is requesting rescinding of protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Let us go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session, Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the beginning of the war and during the war, were you in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when the Serbs took over power in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the 30th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when the attack on Prijedor took place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the 30th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who performed the attack on Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The attack on Prijedor was executed by -- there were these Muslims who attacked Prijedor at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the attack on Prijedor took place, where were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was at home in Donja Puharska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the ethnic composition of the Donja Puharska settlement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anything happen to you on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the 30th of May, in the afternoon, the army came with APCs and buses, and they said that all the men between the ages of 15 to 60 should go out on to the main street in Puharska, and that's what we did. And from there, they put us into the buses and we were taken to Omarska camp. We spent about two hours there, and then were returned to the Keraterm Collection Centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anybody else taken by those buses, of your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, myself and [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, may we have the names [redacted] deleted, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please do not mention the names, witness. Do you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD/5, how long did you stay in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until the 13th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived in Keraterm, where were you put up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Room number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I should like to ask the usher -- I have seven, in fact, albums of photographs from Keraterm, which are identical and numbered. Could the usher please distribute these sets of photographs to all parties; to the Prosecution, the Defence and the Chamber? Mr. President, with your permission for us to be able to follow this exhibit better, the album is numbered K1, runs K1 to K24, and those are photographs from Keraterm. The second part of the album contains photographs from the Omarska Investigation Centre, and they have been numbered 0 until up to 17, I think, from zero to 17. I would like to ask the technical -- the registry to help us with the numbering of the album to facilitate matters, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, let us have them marked for identification, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and for this document, for purposes of identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The registry have just informed me that their computers are not functioning. Perhaps we can use this provisional mark that you have given, and after that, the registry will give us the proper number as soon as her computer becomes operational again. So please proceed, Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD/5, you said that upon your arrival in the Keraterm Investigation Centre you were put in Room 2; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have a photograph numbered K14 in front of you, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I haven't got anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a minute and the usher will find it for you. If you turn to look at the ELMO, Witness, and the document placed there, is this a photograph of the internal part of the compound of the Keraterm Investigation Centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this photograph, as they were taken ten days ago, could you tell the Trial Chamber and everybody else present where Room 2 was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can do that. Room 1 was over here, and behind this container was Room 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's better. We can see the photograph better now, but that is another photograph. That is photograph K15; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you indicate where Room 2 is on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Room 2 was behind this container here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, may the witness be given a magic marker to place an X and a number 2 at the location of that room, or could we go back to the previous photograph, which was numbered K14.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, would you write number 2 on the photograph. Put a 2 on the photograph for the location of the room.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that behind the container, do you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Room 2 was behind that container.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any other rooms there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There were two other rooms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which rooms were those?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Room 3 and Room 4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Room 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was that, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you show us where Room 1 was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please put a number 1 where Room 1 was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD/5, when you arrived at the investigation centre, how many rooms were there where the detainees were accommodated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were two rooms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which two rooms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Room 2 and Room 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, was Room 4 functional?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While I was in Keraterm, Room 4 was only used for the soldiers of Republika Srpska who were detained there and who had fled from the front Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25 lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why you were brought to the Keraterm Investigation Centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we were collected up in front of our homes, we were told that we were going there for questioning, that they would ask us whether we had taken part in the attack on Prijedor, and then they told us that we would be sent home, and that's how it all happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you questioned when you arrived in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was questioned several days after my arrival in the Keraterm Collection Centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who questioned you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The inspectors from Banja Luka did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that questioning, were you physically abused?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to ask the usher's assistance once again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD/5, where were you interrogated during your stay in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the upstairs floor of the building, and the window was on the right-hand side looking out onto the Banja Luka road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should now like to ask the usher for his assistance once again, Mr. President. Could we take out photograph K15 from the album and have it placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD/5, on photograph K15, can you see the room you were questioned in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you indicate with the pointer where it was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was the entrance door, and I went upstairs this way, and this is where that room was where they questioned us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you put a -- the letter "SI" for the interrogation room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, would you place an "SI," an "S" before the "I" for the interrogation room. So was that the interrogation room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was, sir. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Usher. We won't be needing your assistance for the time being. If I do need your assistance again, I'll call upon you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD/5, before the war began in Prijedor municipality, did you know Zigic Zoran?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I knew him before the war, while Zoran Zigic was a taxi driver in the town of Prijedor. He would be at the taxi depot, at the railway station and bus station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you were brought to Keraterm, did you see Zoran Zigic in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him to begin with, when we arrived in Keraterm, and I saw him a few other times as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD/5, do you remember when you saw Zoran Zigic the first time, what he was wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. Zigic, Zoran Zigic, had a camouflage uniform, army boots and a red beret.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether Zoran had any problems with his hand at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did. When we came to the Keraterm Collection Centre, his left hand was bandaged up, and it was bandaged throughout the time that we were in the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what Zoran Zigic did in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zoran Zigic had a minibus and he was in charge of the water and the food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw Zoran in Keraterm, what was his behaviour like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zoran Zigic used to shout at the soldiers and at us detainees as well, but he wasn't aggressive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you were in Keraterm until the 13th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that period of time, did you see Zoran Zigic help the detainees in Keraterm in any way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. He helped them. He gave my brothers cigarettes, and my brothers gave me some -- a cigarette or two, because during the war there weren't any cigarettes. He would bring biscuits and things like that, and he would do that for the other detainees as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you say in addition to the cigarettes? What would he bring?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he would bring biscuits and sweets, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you heard of the surname Curic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were those people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were two Curic brothers, Sadic and Hajrudin, and before the war they had truck -- they were truck drivers and they lived in Musliman Gomjenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Zoran talk to them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened after the conversation with those people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that after that conversation, the two Curic brothers left with Zoran Zigic, they went to their homes, back home, to Musliman Gomjenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did they stay there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were there for a couple of days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they return to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did return to Keraterm. The soldiers brought them and the reserve policemen brought them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know an individual by the name of Faruk Rizvic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was that individual?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Faruk Rizvic lived behind the biscuit factory, and he had a car wash service and a car repair shop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever have occasion to go and fetch water in the minibus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who drove the minibus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zoran Zigic drove it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Faruk Rizvic with you on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to fetch the water from his yard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Rizvic's house there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did Faruk do during that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, during that time, Faruk would go home and have a bath, have a change of clothing, and while we were pouring the water into the canisters, we were -- sat around in his yard and had something to eat and drink.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD/5?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I hear you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a person by the name of Sead Jusufagic, nicknamed Car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was Sead Jusufovic, nicknamed Car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you tell us his full -- his surname?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sead Jusufovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And his nickname?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His nickname was Car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe him? Did you know him from before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He was a neighbour of mine, and before the war, he spent some time in prisons and detention centres, reformatories. He was a bit of a problem. He was tall, he was thin, he was fair, he didn't have much of his teeth left. He had very few teeth, both on his upper jaw and lower jaw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see that person in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I saw him several days after I arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember who brought Car to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Car was brought to Keraterm by the police and a police van, a 53.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean by a 53? What's a 53?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, when Car was captured, not far from Prijedor, Hambarine, Ljubija, I mean a -- the old type of 53 machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After Car was brought into Keraterm -- actually, can you remember when he was brought to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he was brought sometime before nightfall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after Car was brought to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When they brought Car into Keraterm and when they took him out of the police van, he started straight away in the compound in front of our rooms, he started to run around carrying this 53 machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In front of which rooms was he running?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Between number 1 and number 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who forced him to run?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Duca Knezevic and some reserve policemen and soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Zoran Zigic among the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw Zigic once while Car was there when he kicked him in the behind once, and then Zoran Zigic turned around and left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember, did Zoran Zigic say anything to Car at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far were you from the spot where Car was running?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Five or six metres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you watch the incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said a moment ago that Zoran kicked him. Where did he go after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He went off towards the base. And as far as I can remember, I think he had a small motorcycle. He got on it and left the compound, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this incident, did you see Zoran Zigic beating this man at any time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the days that followed, was Car beaten again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Car was beaten every day for about four consecutive days until he succumbed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Car beaten during the daytime or during the nighttime, or both?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was beaten during the daytime and at night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At night, were you locked up in your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How could you know that Car was being beaten by Zoran at night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't say that Zoran beat Car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. How do you know that Car was being beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We could hear the names being called out, and there was only one wall separating the two rooms and we could hear it, and we could hear the moans and how he was being mistreated and beaten up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know any of the persons who beat Car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did know the Banovic brothers, Duca Knezevic, and Ivica Janjic -- Nikica Janjic, sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember after these beatings what Car looked like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he got worse and worse, and eventually he succumbed to the beatings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After how many days did Car pass away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About four or five days later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when Car was beaten for the last time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was on the 7th or 8th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What month was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who beat him on that occasion, and do you know what the immediate cause was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that the soldiers were saying while beating him that he was found with the 53 rifle and that many policemen had been killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Car when he died?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a little way off, near Room 3 and 4, but we didn't see him, but only in the morning when they opened up the rooms, I heard from the soldiers saying that Car had died.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that Car was called out at night and beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear Zoran Zigic call out Car at night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you have recognised his voice if Zoran Zigic had called out Car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course I would.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD/5, do you know a person by the name of Emsud Bahonjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was he from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he brought to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know approximately when Bahonjic was brought to Keraterm? Just make a pause before giving your answer, please. Can you answer my question now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, he was brought in on the 8th or the 9th, of June again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who brought Emsud Bahonjic to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was Duca Knezevic who brought him to Keraterm, in his car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what kind of car it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was an old model of a green Mercedes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether Emsud Bahonjic was brought to Keraterm with a weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He had a Singapore type rifle on him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how they called Emsud Bahonjic in Keraterm in those days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They called it Singapurka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which room Emsud Bahonjic was placed in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Room 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After he was brought to Keraterm, what happened to Emsud Bahonjic, do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that when he was brought in, he was beaten a little by Duca Knezevic and a couple of other soldiers, and then Duca said that he had killed his late brother Igor. Emsud Bahonjic denied it. And when Duca went to the Trnopolje Collection Centre and brought over his mother, father, wife, and child ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When he brought from Trnopolje, his wife, mother and father, and child, then Duca said that he would slaughter his child if he didn't admit that he had killed his brother Igor. Bahonjic said, "Don't hurt my family. I did kill your brother Igor and cut off his head." However, Duca Knezevic put his family back in the car and took them back to Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that Bahonjic mentioned another name on that occasion --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- that took part in the killing of Duca's brother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Just a moment for me to try and remember. It was one of his neighbours. I can't remember his name now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened later, after this incident with Bahonjic? Was he beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether Emsud Bahonjic was taken to the general hospital in Prijedor and treated there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do. He was taken to the Prijedor hospital and brought back the same day from the Prijedor hospital to the Keraterm Collection Centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where Emsud Bahonjic was beaten? Was it in the room he was in or in the compound?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Emsud Bahonjic was beaten inside the room and in the compound of Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Zoran Zigic beating this man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Zoran Zigic being present there when other persons beat Emsud Bahonjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who mostly beat Emsud Bahonjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Duca Knezevic, soldiers and reserve policemen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And also, when you were transferred to Omarska, did Emsud Bahonjic remain in Keraterm alive? Was he still alive when you left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't know what happened after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were you transferred to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the 13th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Emsud Bahonjic alive when you left Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD/5, during your stay in Keraterm, did you ever meet or hear a person called Jasmin Izeiri?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I just heard of Sedo Duraj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was he by ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a Siptar, an Albanian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to Duraj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that six or seven days later, Duraj was released from Keraterm and that he left altogether for good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who released him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your stay in Keraterm, did you see a person by the name of Fajzo Mujkanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that man from before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know Mujkanovic from before because he came from the same place my father was from, and that is Kozarusa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he look like?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic, we are now going to have a break. Perhaps this is a good time to do that. I'm going to ask the usher to accompany the witness out. Witness, we are now going to have a break. So we now have a half-hour break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Usher, can you bring the witness, please. Mr. Deretic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD/5, could you please briefly describe the physical appearance of Fajzo Mujkanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was short in height, well-built, heavily-built. He wore glasses, and he had slightly longer hair.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what he did before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the war, Mujkanovic was a caterer in the catering business.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After he was brought to Keraterm, do you know whether he had any conflict with anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When he was brought to the Keraterm camp, he had a tiff with Duca Knezevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the war, Duca Knezevic was also a caterer, and they had some unsettled accounts between them. They had a quarrel over money.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did that conflict end? Was it a verbal dispute or a physical one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a verbal dispute, and then Duca slapped Fajzo Mujkanovic once or twice. And before Fajzo was brought to the Keraterm camp, Fajzo was cut across the neck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, when this dispute broke out between Fajzo and Duca, was Zoran Zigic present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Zoran Zigic at any time beating Fajzo Mujkanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to Fajzo Mujkanovic later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The story was that Fajzo Mujkanovic was transferred --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Slow down, please. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that Fajzo was later transferred to the Trnopolje Collection Centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether Fajzo Mujkanovic survived this investigation centre? Is he alive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is certainly alive. He's in a third country today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD/5, did you know a person called Jasmin Ramadanovic known as Sengin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was he from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jasmin Ramadanovic before the war had his own coffee bar in town, opposite Ramo's sweet shop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe him, his appearance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jasmin was of medium height. He had lengthy hair, and he had a receding hairline. He was quite stocky.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether he was in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when he was brought to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he was brought in at the very outset.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he physically mistreated after arriving?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who beat him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that the Banovic brothers beat him, Duca Knezevic, and Ivica Janjic, and there were some other soldiers there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Zigic beating Ramadanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether Ramadanovic was taken to hospital for treatment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when he returned from hospital and whether Ramadanovic returned from hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do know that he returned from the hospital to the Keraterm camp, I think after two or three days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to him later on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I couldn't tell because I was transferred to the Omarska camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD/5, do you know a person called Drago Tokmadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Drago Tokmadzic before the war was a policeman in Ljubija and Prijedor, and he worked at the bus and railway station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what kind of a policeman he was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a poor policeman before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean "poor"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On one occasion as I was passing through the bus and railway station, I saw Drago Tokmadzic in a cafe, which still exists in Prijedor, beating him and insulting him, and many passersby watched it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember when Drago Tokmadzic was brought in whether you were in the compound?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was in my room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him being brought in, from your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. He was brought in, in a police van.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was wearing the old police uniform and a cap on his head with a five-cornered star.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After Drago Tokmadzic was brought in, what room was he put in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was put, I think, in Room 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure whether he was in that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure, but I think -- no, no. May I correct myself? He was put in Room 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wait a minute, Witness, please. Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That's leading. I've tried to be patient with some of it, but I think this was pretty excessive, and to inform the witness through signalling about the direction of testimony is inappropriate. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I just repeated the question, asking the witness whether he was sure, in view of the fact that the witness himself said that he wasn't quite sure whether it was Room number 1. It was not at all my intention to lead at all. I just wanted to check whether the witness was sure about this fact. That was all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Continue, Mr. Deretic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, after Drago Tokmadzic was brought in, do you know what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as all of us detainees could see, he was also beaten and mistreated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was he beaten; during the day or during the night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Both during the day and during the night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Zoran Zigic beating this man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Zoran Zigic being anywhere in the vicinity when this man was being beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Drago Tokmadzic? Did he stay on in Keraterm after you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he alive when you left Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to him later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't say. I was in the camp, in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD/5, you said that you were transferred from Keraterm to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us again what date that was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 13th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time of the day or night were you transferred to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you transferred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A police van took me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what the weather was like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a lot of rain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean that particular day or generally during that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it rained heavily on that day when I was transferred, and over the next few days as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anybody else transferred to Omarska with you on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, 12 of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived in Omarska, where were you put up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was taken to the "white house."

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to ask the usher for his assistance. May we have a photograph placed on the ELMO? It is number O8, photograph O8.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us what this building is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the so-called "white house" where we were put up when we were brought there. That's where they put us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What room were you in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first room to the left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see the windows of that room on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said a moment -- you used a marker pen a moment ago but it was a very thick one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have a thinner marker, so may I give that to the usher so that the witness can mark in the various positions with that thinner marker?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, would you put an X on the window of the room that you were put in.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were put into that particular room, did the room have glass on the windows or was it planks and glass?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. There was glass all over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were brought to that room, did you find anybody already there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. There were several of the people who were brought there from Kozarac, like me. Five or six people were there already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were these people -- what was their position? Were they standing up or lying down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some of them were sitting down on the tiles. One of them was lying down. And another was beaten up. He had been abused and beaten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know any of those people in that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I knew Hankin. They called him Hankin. Ramic, Sead Ramic, that is; I think that was his proper name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his nickname?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hankin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell us, please, who was the man lying down or who was half lying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On that first day, towards evening, I asked the young men who the man was, and they said that it was Becir, Medunjanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what Becir Medunjanin looked like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was all broken on the left-hand side. He had a cut over -- across his nose and he had a plaster on his nose.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the plaster clean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, no. It was all bloody and ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were brought to that room and put up there, were you questioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The second day, after the second day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I was beaten when I went up for interrogation to the Omarska camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to ask the usher to place a photograph on the ELMO, and it is photograph number O5, and you can take it out of the album. We can see better that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic, I have been informed that the ELMO is working -- not working properly [as interpreted], and the registry says it's functioning, so we must establish a correspondence between the photographs already shown and this one. Madam Registrar, can you now give us the proper number for identification for this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. The first picture that was shown I believe was K14, and that will be marked D10/4. The next exhibit shown was K15, and that will be marked D11/4. The next picture shown was O8, and that is marked for identification D12/4. And this exhibit number that's on the ELMO, O5, will be D13/4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Deretic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD/5, on this picture O5, can you indicate the room you were interrogated in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can. The entrance was here. You go in here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you speak up, please. Where is the entrance to the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The entrance is here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the ELMO, please, on the photograph itself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is where the entrance is, and I was interrogated up on this floor. I think it was this room here, the third or fourth window.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do these windows look out onto the pista of the investigation centre of Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you now place a letter, an X, on the window.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us who interrogated you in that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was interrogated by the inspectors from Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you physically mistreated during those interrogations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What room were you taken back to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On that day when they had interrogated me, I was taken back to the "white house" again, and as I went the second day for interrogation again ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got to the "white house" and were put up there, were you physically mistreated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Becir Medunjanin mistreated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes. Before I came and during the time I spent there, he was mistreated as well. He was beaten, and they said he was the main organiser of the attack on Prijedor from Kozarac, that kind of thing. That's what they said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who beat you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was beaten by Duca Knezevic and two other soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you went back for interrogation the second day; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after that second time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, when I went off to be interrogated for the next time, I knelt in front of the inspector on my knees, and on my head I had one of those plastic yoghurt cups on my head, full of water. Now, if the water were to spill, I would be beaten. And an inspector turned up from Prijedor who worked with my sister in the GIK Mrakovica company in Prijedor, and he looked at me, took one look at me, and said, "Are you Zeric?" And I said yes. And then he swore at the inspectors and said, "Well, I guarantee for that man. That man is a poor man, and he's not involved in anything, in the attack and things like that." And then he took me by the hand and took me downstairs to the pista and we -- I went back to the "white house," and I spent the night there, that night -- that is to say, I was released before nightfall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you were released from that room --

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I should like to ask for the usher's assistance again and place photograph O17 on the ELMO, and then O16 after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Madam Registrar, may we have an identification number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. O17 will be marked D14/4, and the next exhibit, O16, will be marked D15/4.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does photograph O14 show the entrance when you go into the "white house," what you see upon entering?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The room marked O16, O16, is that the room you were in, O16?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the first one on the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the ELMO we see a photograph marked O17. I would like to have O16 placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the room you were put up in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anything in the room like the things we see on the photograph now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the photograph, can you see the actual position and place you were in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you show us that, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that a place underneath the window?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was, in the very corner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you place -- could you write in "DD/5" in that particular position, write the letters and number DD/5.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were sitting down there, could you see out of the window?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How high was the room from the floor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About a metre.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The window from the floor, the interpreter apologises. "How high was the window from the floor?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to Becir Medunjanin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do know what happened to Becir Medunjanin. Duca Knezevic turned up with two soldiers, and they were -- provided security for the Omarska camp, and they took Becir by the arm and took him outside in front of the "white house," and they continued to abuse him, to beat him, until Becir Medunjanin fell down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us when that happened, how many days after your arrival in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I arrived in Omarska on the 13th of June, and that happened about the 16th or 17th of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because the interpretation wasn't precise enough, could you tell us once again, repeat once again -- you said he succumbed. What do you mean by "succumbed"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was all beaten up. And he had died, in fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us more specifically what time of day or night it was when this happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was at about 1800 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you -- were you able to see Becir's body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, when he was already killed, his body was there for about two hours. I saw his body for about two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I should like to ask the usher to show us photograph O12 now and place it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: O12 will be marked Exhibit D16/4.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We now have photograph O12 on the ELMO. Could you put an X at the place where Becir Medunjanin was taken out and where his body lay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was in this room here. This is the door. They took him out this way. And this is where he lay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD/5, you said that when you came to the "white house," Hankin -- Ramic, nicknamed Hankin, was there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ramic went out with Duca Knezevic and several other soldiers before Becir. But he was taken to the left-hand side when he was taken out of the "white house," and I think that Hankin Ramic was killed because he never returned to the so-called "white house."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this photograph, O12, could you indicate where Hankin was taken out to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can. He was taken out through this door, taken this way to the left, across this little path, and at the very edge of the building, this is where he was. I couldn't actually see him from my room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you place X1 -- an X1 at that spot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here, it is, yes, X1. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see him from where you were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know he was taken to the left of the door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I know that because I could see the path, and he didn't go down the path, or he wasn't by Becir, either, but he was to the other side. Duca and the two or three other soldiers said, "Bring him here to the left." I heard them say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Hankin return to your room afterwards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this event took place, how long did you stay on in the "white house"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they released me when Becir succumbed, that is to say when he was killed, and Hankin, too, and I was taken out at about 2000 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the same time when this happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you taken out of the "white house" then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was taken out on to the pista, in the compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher place photograph O4 on the ELMO now, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Photograph O4 is Exhibit D17/4.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are now looking at photograph O4. Could you take up your marker and place a P at the spot you were taken to and where you were put up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can. What letter did you say?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I said the letter P. Write in a P, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much time did you spend at that particular spot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was there the whole time, until we were transferred to the Trnopolje Collection Centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic, I think it is up to you to define something here. Was the witness at the top of the letter or the bottom of the letter, because that is a very broad angle of vision. The P takes up a lot of space. So the upper part of the P is almost by the left-hand building, but that's up to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, Mr. President. You're quite right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD/5, could you tell us more precisely how far away from the wall of this left-hand building you were, how many metres away from that big building on the left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean from the hangar?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there was the first row of us, there were about 40 or 50 people, and then there was a second row, a third row and a fourth row. We were up by the hangar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which row were you in, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in row number 2, in the second row, at the very corner to the "white house."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many metres were you away from the wall of this large hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About two or three metres away from the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, would that be sufficient indication in view of the letter P marking? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were there in Keraterm for the first four or five days, did you ever see Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During my stay there, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I would see him around. I saw him several times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking about Omarska.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him at all in Omarska, not once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am saying in the first four or five days that you were in the "white house," that's what I'm asking you about. And when you went out onto the pista, did you ever see Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. You asked me, sir, about Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise, witness. That was my mistake. I stand corrected. In view of the fact that you were moved after four or five days to the pista, could it have happened that Zoran Zigic came into the compound of the Omarska Investigation Centre without you seeing him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that couldn't happen. It couldn't happen that nobody saw him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could it happen that he came in by night without you hearing him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we were there the whole time. All the time we were in the camp we spent out on the pista and it was warm, the weather was warm, so we were outside and we would have heard him if he came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were you let out of Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the beginning of August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go after Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went to the Trnopolje Collection Centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much time did you spend there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Between 15 and 20 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that time, did you see Zoran Zigic in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you left Trnopolje, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in my own house in Donja Puharska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your house destroyed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until when did you stay in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until the 17th of September, 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you were released from Trnopolje until the 17th of September, 1994, what did you do and where were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was mobilised to a work platoon and, with the army of Republika Srpska, I went digging trenches and dugouts and that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could I now request that we go into private session for my next series of questions, because otherwise I fear that the identity of this witness could easily be disclosed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the suggestion is a good one, so let us take a break, which will give you a chance to organise yourself, and we'll return in 50 minutes' time. But would the usher show the witness out of the courtroom first before we adjourn for 50 minutes. A 50-minute lunch break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Yes, Ms. Susan Somers, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you. If we are still in private session, I will address the questions that would be private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would ask, then, for a few minutes in private session. I have just a couple -- several questions, not lengthy, and there are two exhibits which I think will require, for purposes of not necessarily having them broadcast to the public gallery, just because of identification, if possible private session for a moment, but I'll try to ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, let us go into private session for a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are, Ms. Susan Somers, please continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated after having spent some nine or so days, or perhaps 13 days, in Omarska -- in Keraterm, where you were beaten but you were also trusted to spend periods of time outside of the camp, you indicated you were sent to Omarska. Did any other members of your family also go to Omarska, or only you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I got to Omarska, I found my late brother there. He was rounded up on the 30th of May, 1992. He was not far from the house, on the main road, on the Prijedor-Bosanski Novi road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Without giving any names, that particular sibling was not in Keraterm; is that correct? Was always in Omarska, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the time when he was picked up from the main road, he was immediately taken to the Omarska camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were at Keraterm, did you sell cigarettes and food products to other detainees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My brother sold cigarettes, and some food was sold too. When we got to Keraterm, Zigic Zoran gave us cigarettes and food free.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was it those cigarettes and that food that you -- that was sold to the other detainees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you yourself at any time sell any cigarettes in any amount or any food in any amount to any detainee?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I did sell some cigarettes. That was for about an hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do with the money from the sale of those cigarettes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I may have sold two or three boxes only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do with the money from the sale of those boxes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A soldier came up, I can't remember his name now, the one who had brought me those cigarettes to sell, so I didn't sell them all, and I gave him back the packets I hadn't sold and the money for the two or three packets I had sold.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was a soldier who brought you the cigarettes from Zigic, the go-between, as it were, the intermediary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to make sure I understand this. After you had spent time in Keraterm, and you were trusted sufficiently to be out of the camp with Zigic and to turn money over to Zigic, you were then sent to Omarska to the "white house" where, according to evidence or suggestion, the worst of the detainees, the most dangerous, in the eyes of the Serb authorities, were held. Why, in your mind, were you, a trusted man, put in that environment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am trying to be extremely tolerant and to avoid interrupting my learned friend, but I really don't understand how far this may be allowed to go. If my learned colleague mentions the Investigation Centre in Omarska and says that the worst detainees were held there, that is a conclusion. Never once did the witness say anything like that. He never even described the kind of detainees that were sent to Omarska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: It is necessary to be concise. [Interpretation] Yes, Ms. Susan Somers, if you look at your question, there are many judgements in it. So perhaps you should rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Evidence has been brought before this Chamber that some of the worst beatings, and frequently fatal beatings, took place in the "white house" out of the view of the general population of the detainees at Omarska. Can you help us understand why you were put in that particular structure where this type of activity took place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I was interrogated in the Keraterm camp, and when they completed the interrogation, they suspected that I had taken part in the attack on Prijedor and that I have my own weapon. That's it. That's all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it that you were sent, as it were, as a spy, to watch and monitor activity among persons in Omarska? Is that what really happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking back at Exhibit 3/251, which I would ask not to be put on the ELMO out of privacy concerns, I'd like to ask you, please -- you mentioned on the bottom of English page 2, and I think it would be on your page -- possibly on your page 2 as well. Yes, it is. There is a discussion about events at the end of July, 1992. Paragraph begins: "A man known as Zigo, a taxi driver from Prijedor, in the vicinity of Prijedor by birth, I know he held a rank in the Chetnik army, was in Omarska throughout this time. He was notorious for beating," et cetera. That is the paragraph I'm reading from. If you look down --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Witness DD/5 has explicitly stated under which circumstances he made this statement, and it is our submission that any questions related to this statement is unfair and inappropriate and pointless.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Susan Somers, your response?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The Chamber can take into consideration the amount of weight it wishes to give the statement and the general circumstances surrounding all aspects of this individual's arrest and detention, but I think the relevance certainly is there. I do not think there would be any basis for not proceeding with questions from here, and if the Chamber deems there to be some aspect of the statement that may give it pause, then it would take consideration of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It would be very easy to say to Ms. Susan Somers to continue, but I think the Chamber, as always, wishes to explain its decision. It would be easy for a witness to say that, "I gave this statement under such and such a condition" without the party that is cross-examining him being able to check the credibility of that witness through that statement.
